Upstream payments provider degradation c.challenged_claim: An upstream payments provider degradation was the sole cause of the checkout 502 spike.

counterclaims.statement: Our integration has no local retry or backoff on charge.create, so our own design choices shaped how the provider degradation reached users.

evidence_gaps: The specific charge.create call pattern that may have worsened the provider timeouts is not captured.
falsification_tests: Correlate the provider 504 timestamps against our 502 spike to confirm the provider led rather than followed.

Missing client-side retry and backoff am.challenged_claim: Missing client-side retry and backoff was the dominant amplifier of the checkout failures.

counterclaims.statement: Checkout error rate recovered as soon as the provider recovered, suggesting provider availability, not retry policy, drove the outage duration.

evidence_gaps: How many 502s a bounded retry would have absorbed is unknown without a replay.
falsification_tests: Replay the provider timeout window against a retry-enabled client in staging and measure absorbed failures.

A local checkout deploy regressed paymen.challenged_claim: A local checkout deploy regressed payments handling and caused the 502s.

counterclaims.statement: No deploy went out on the incident day, so a local code regression is unlikely.

evidence_gaps: The checkout service deploy log around 09:00-09:10 has not been audited for out-of-band changes.
falsification_tests: Audit the deploy and config-change log for the checkout service across 09:00-09:10.
